newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate leader concerned by CIA-Iraq operation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate leader concerned by CIA-Iraq operation.

text.p: U.S. Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott expressed concern on Sunday over reports that a secret CIA operation was foiled last week by Saddam Hussein's assault on Kurds in northern Iraq.

"That whole operation concerns me," Lott told Reuters after addressing the annual meeting of the Southern Governors' Association. "I do think the intelligence committee should ask some questions about it."
Lott stopped short off calling for a full-scale Senate investigation into the operation but said he would ask for a report from Sen. Arlen Specter, chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee.
The New York Times reported on Saturday that a handful of CIA officers in northern Iraq had fled last week as Iraqi forces occupied the city of Arbil.
The Washington Post reported on Sunday that 100 Iraqis associated with the CIA efforts had apparently been arrested and executed by forces supporting Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein.

"I want to know what the circumstances were for their being withdrawn. What did we do to those that were working with us? Did we expose them to what has now been their apparent execution? I'm not condemning it, I just want to know what the deal is," Lott said.

Newspaper reports said President Bill Clinton expanded the covert operation in January, signing a secret order directing the CIA to provide weapons and military training and install intelligence-gathering equipment for Saddam's opponents.

The Los Angeles Times reported on Sunday that CIA Director John Deutch had promised Iraqi dissidents that Saddam would be overthrown within a year, but the Iraqi leader discovered and foiled the $20-million covert operation to unseat him.
The paper quoted a senior U.S. official saying this was one of the worst setbacks ever suffered by U.S. intelligence.
Last week, Lott complained that the White House had failed to notify or consult congressional leaders before it launched the first wave of U.S. missile attacks against Iraqi targets last Tuesday.
But Lott said on Sunday that White House and National Security Council officials had responded to his complaints and been keeping him informed of subsequent developments in the region.
Lott said the War Powers Act requires the president to notify and consult with Congress prior to approving any military operation.

The United States fired cruise missile at air defence targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday after Baghdad troops helped a Kurdish group seize the northern town of Arbil from a rival faction.
